question.name: Question 2
question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & 0 \\ 8 & -3 & 0 \\ 4 & -4 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

If the matrix $A$ above is diagonalizable, find a corresponding diagonal matrix $D.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the eigenvalues of the matrix $A$ by solving $det(A-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & 1 & 0 \\ 8 & -3-\lambda  & 0 \\ 4 & -4 & 5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (5-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & 1 \\ 8 & -3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (5-\lambda )((4-\lambda )(-3-\lambda )-8) & =0 \\ -(\lambda -5)({\lambda }^{2}-\lambda -20) & =0 \\ (\lambda -5)(\lambda +4)(\lambda -5) & =0 \\ (\lambda +4)(\lambda -5)^{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}=-4$ (simple root) and ${\lambda }_{2}=5$ (double root).

Let's now find the dimension of the eigenspace corresponding to each eigenvalue.

- First, we consider the simple root ${\lambda }_{1}=-4.$ Since the root is simple, the dimension of the eigenspace ${V}_{-4}$ corresponding to ${\lambda }_{1}=-4$ is

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{-4})=1.
$$

- Next, we consider the double root ${\lambda }_{2}=5.$ Let's find the dimension of the eigenspace ${V}_{5}$ corresponding to this eigenvalue. To do this, we row-reduce the matrix $A-5I:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-5I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & 0 \\ 8 & -3 & 0 \\ 4 & -4 & 5\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 8 & -8 & 0 \\ 4 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+8{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). This implies that we will have $3-1=2$ linearly independent eigenvectors corresponding to ${\lambda }_{2}=5.$ So,

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{5})=2.
$$

Therefore, $A$ is diagonalizable, since

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{-4})+\text{dim}({V}_{5})=1+2=3.\,✓
$$

Finally, a corresponding diagonal matrix is 

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the eigenvalues of the matrix $A$ by solving $det(A-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & 1 & 0 \\ 8 & -3-\lambda  & 0 \\ 4 & -4 & 5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (5-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & 1 \\ 8 & -3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (5-\lambda )((4-\lambda )(-3-\lambda )-8) & =0 \\ -(\lambda -5)({\lambda }^{2}-\lambda -20) & =0 \\ (\lambda -5)(\lambda +4)(\lambda -5) & =0 \\ (\lambda +4)(\lambda -5)^{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}=-4$ (simple root) and ${\lambda }_{2}=5$ (double root).

Let's now find the dimension of the eigenspace corresponding to each eigenvalue.

- First, we consider the simple root ${\lambda }_{1}=-4.$ Since the root is simple, the dimension of the eigenspace ${V}_{-4}$ corresponding to ${\lambda }_{1}=-4$ is

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{-4})=1.
$$

- Next, we consider the double root ${\lambda }_{2}=5.$ Let's find the dimension of the eigenspace ${V}_{5}$ corresponding to this eigenvalue. To do this, we row-reduce the matrix $A-5I:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-5I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & 0 \\ 8 & -3 & 0 \\ 4 & -4 & 5\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 8 & -8 & 0 \\ 4 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+8{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). This implies that we will have $3-1=2$ linearly independent eigenvectors corresponding to ${\lambda }_{2}=5.$ So,

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{5})=2.
$$

Therefore, $A$ is diagonalizable, since

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{-4})+\text{dim}({V}_{5})=1+2=3.\,✓
$$

Finally, a corresponding diagonal matrix is 

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$
